page.title: Field app prototype
page.heading: The field app: a clickable prototype
page.about: The key screens of the field app, built from its own components and look: home, a collection, the tower, a unit rate ticket and sending your work. The records are the example world’s, made up; nothing is saved or sent.

screens.tower: Kim Nguyen: the tower at Marsh Road TDSR

page.designsAbout: Each choice below changes the screens. The first of each is the agent’s recommendation. None is built into the app until you answer (spec/QUESTIONS.md, Q-215 to Q-218).

confirm.label: 1. A confirmation after each value
confirm.about: Build 1’s board asked “You have selected 55%. Is that correct?” after every pick. It costs a tap per value, many trucks an hour; the review screen before the number checks everything once.
confirm.no: No: the review screen checks it all once (recommended)

count.label: 2. A monitor scorecard
count.about: What the monitor sees of their own day. The agent suggests their own count of today’s tickets on home, nothing ranked or compared; reports on monitors belong to the back office.

menu.label: 3. The bottom menu
menu.about: Build 1’s board had Time, Map, Work, Chats and Settings. No phase’s requirements put a map or chats on the phone.
menu.trimmed: Work, Time (where the clock is on), Sync, Settings (recommended)
menu.board: Build 1’s board: Time, Map, Work, Chats, Settings
menu.none: No menu: home and the status strip only

again.label: 4. Typing the ticket number again
again.about: Today the number is always typed again by hand, after a scan too (ADR-209). WCAG 2.2’s 3.3.7 (Redundant Entry) lets a second entry stand only where it is essential. Typing again a number a person copied checks the copy, as a memory test does: essential. Typing again a number the scanner read checks nothing a person copied.
again.byHand: Only when a person copied it: a phone-made number, or one typed because the barcode won’t read (recommended)
again.always: Always, after a scan too (as ADR-209 says today)

page.stop: This part is not in the prototype.

flow.printed: Printed. The driver takes their copy.
flow.saved: Ticket {number} is saved on this phone. It sends when there’s signal.
flow.sealed: Submitted, so it can’t be changed on the phone. The back office corrects it if it needs it.

today.one: Today: 1 ticket made on this phone
today.other: Today: {count} tickets made on this phone

badge.label: Badge number
badge.unknown: Badge {number} isn’t in this phone’s lists. Keep going: the truck is keyed in by hand, and the ticket is flagged for review.

loading.title: The truck is loading
loading.started: Started {time}. Complete the load when the truck is full.

photos.title: Photos
photos.required: This work asks for photos. Without one the ticket is flagged for review; you can still go on.

review.title: Check the ticket
review.right: It’s right: on to the number

number.shownAbout: Note it as your firm asks. You type it again on the next screen.
number.typed: A typed number is flagged for review, with its reason.
number.wrong: That isn’t this ticket’s number. Check it and type it again.

call.title: How full is the truck?
call.high: {call}% is at or over this project’s {limit}%, so it is flagged for review. Carry on if it’s right.
call.low: {call}% is at or under this project’s {limit}%, so it is flagged for review. Carry on if it’s right.
call.zero: 0% bills nothing and is flagged for review. Carry on if it’s right.
call.over: A load call is at most 100%.

unitRate.onlySome: The prototype goes on with Hangers and Leaners only.

sync.title: Send your work

events.none: No field events wait on this phone.
events.one: 1 field event waits on this phone.
events.other: {count} field events wait on this phone.

photos.none: No photos wait on this phone.

sync.quarantined: A second disposal on ticket {number}. It is kept for the back office to sort out; nothing is lost.
sync.refreshed: The lists are up to date.
